games.title: Mafia (party game)
games.note: Created by psychology student Dmitry Davidoff at Moscow State University; it spread through dorms and summer camps.

games.title: Werewolf (party game)
games.note: Andrew Plotkin re-themed Mafia with werewolves in 1997, arguing they suited a hidden enemy better.

games.title: Town of Salem
games.note: An online Mafia set during the Salem witch trials.

games.title: Among Us
games.note: Released in 2018 to little notice; streamers made it a hit in 2020, when it peaked at 3.8 million concurrent players.

games.title: Fall Guys
games.note: Lead designer Joe Walsh's pitch reminded him of the TV game shows Takeshi's Castle and Total Wipeout.

games.title: Lethal Company
games.note: A solo developer's early-access hit; PC Gamer likened it to a more chaotic and deadly Phasmophobia.

games.title: Content Warning
games.dev: Landfall team (Wilnyl, Philip, thePetHen, Skog, Zorro)
games.note: Made mostly during an internal Landfall game jam in Seoul and released on April Fools' Day 2024.

games.title: R.E.P.O.
games.note: Launched in Steam early access in February 2025 by the small Swedish studio semiwork.

games.title: Peak
games.note: Began as a one-month game jam in South Korea and sold over 10 million copies by August 2025.

games.title: Goat Simulator
games.note: Began as a joke game-jam prototype; its alpha footage drew over a million YouTube views in two days.

games.title: Satisfactory
games.note: Early access began in March 2019; version 1.0 arrived in September 2024.

games.title: Human: Fall Flat
games.note: Made by Lithuanian developer Tomas Sakalauskas; it has sold over 58 million copies.

games.title: Cocoon
games.note: Directed by Jeppe Carlsen, who designed Playdead's Limbo and Inside before leaving in 2016.

games.title: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
games.note: Directed by Swedish-Lebanese filmmaker Josef Fares; each thumbstick controls one of the two brothers.

games.title: A Way Out
games.note: A prison escape that can only be played by two people, in split screen.

games.title: It Takes Two
games.note: Won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2021 and sold over 30 million copies by April 2026.

games.title: Split Fiction
games.note: Sold over a million copies in its first two days in March 2025.

games.title: Magicka
games.note: Began as a project by eight students at Luleå University of Technology in Skellefteå.

games.title: Helldivers 2
games.note: Sold over 19 million copies by October 2025, according to Sony and Arrowhead.

games.title: Palworld
games.note: Sold 8 million copies in its first six days of early access in January 2024; version 1.0 followed in July 2026.

games.title: Schedule I
games.note: A solo Australian developer's early-access drug-empire sim that briefly drew more Steam players than GTA V.

games.title: Sifu
games.note: Its combat is based on the Bak Mei kung fu style, and each death ages the hero.

games.title: Rematch
games.note: Sloclap's five-a-side football game reached 3 million players within its first week in June 2025.

links.took: Mafia's rules: a hidden minority kills at night, and the town votes by day.
links.added: Werewolves, which Andrew Plotkin argued fit an enemy who looks normal by day.

links.took: Mafia's hidden roles, night kills and daytime votes.
links.added: Online games set in the Salem witch trials, with many special roles.

src.t: Wikipedia: Town of Salem, citing TheGamer, 2019

links.took: Hidden killers in a group who must talk and vote them out.
links.added: Spaceship chores, emergency meetings and sabotage, played online with friends.

src.t: Wikipedia: Among Us, citing Gamasutra and PC Gamer, 2020

links.extra: Innersloth's Marcus Bromander, who conceived it, had played Mafia since childhood; the film The Thing was another influence.

links.took: PUBG popularized battle royales where dozens enter and one wins.
links.added: Obstacle-course game-show rounds instead of guns, with clumsy jellybean characters.
links.extra: Mediatonic set it apart from shooter battle royales by drawing on TV game shows such as Takeshi's Castle.

links.took: Phasmophobia popularized co-op horror where friends hear each other through proximity voice chat.
links.added: Scavenging abandoned moons for scrap to meet a corporate quota.
links.extra: Reviewers compared the two; PC Gamer called it a more chaotic and deadly Phasmophobia.

links.took: Friends exploring a monster-filled place together, talking by proximity voice.
links.added: Filming the scares to go viral on an in-game video site.

src.t: Wikipedia: Content Warning, citing mxdwn Games

links.took: Co-op horror scavenging to meet a quota, with proximity voice.
links.added: Physics-based hauling of fragile valuables out of haunted buildings.

src.t: Wikipedia: R.E.P.O., citing PC Gamer and GamesRadar+, 2025

links.extra: PC Gamer described the gameplay as similar to Lethal Company; GamesRadar+ said it had the spirit of Lethal Company.

links.took: Landfall's practice of making small co-op games at jams in South Korea.
links.added: A cooperative mountain climb with stamina, ropes and rescues.

links.took: Aggro Crab, the studio behind Another Crab's Treasure, as co-developer.
links.added: A co-op climbing game that outsold the studio's previous game within a week.

links.took: Skating-game scoring: chaining stunts for points.
links.added: A goat that wrecks things instead of doing tricks, in a deliberately silly physics sandbox.

src.t: Wikipedia: Goat Simulator, citing Armin Ibrisagic in Polygon, 2014

links.extra: Lead designer Armin Ibrisagic called it an old-school skating game where you play a goat that wrecks stuff.

links.took: Coffee Stain's Unreal Engine experience from Goat Simulator and Sanctum.
links.added: A first-person factory-building game on an alien planet.

links.took: Goat mayhem and physics comedy.
links.added: Four-player online play; the developers skipped the 2 as a joke.

links.took: Building and automating ever-larger factories.
links.added: A first-person 3D world to explore and build in.

src.t: Wikipedia: Satisfactory, citing Rock Paper Shotgun (2018) and Eurogamer (2019)

links.extra: Rock Paper Shotgun said it looked a lot like first-person Factorio.

links.took: The original aim: a physics puzzle game in Portal's vein.
links.added: A wobbly, hard-to-control hero whose clumsiness became the comedy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Human: Fall Flat, citing Tomas Sakalauskas in TheGamer

links.took: The original aim of a moody puzzle game like Limbo.
links.added: Loose physics puzzles with many solutions, often played with friends.

src.t: Wikipedia: Human: Fall Flat, citing Tomas Sakalauskas in TheGamer

links.extra: Playtesting with his son pushed Sakalauskas to lean into the physics instead of watertight puzzles.

links.took: Playdead's dark, wordless puzzle-platforming.
links.added: A 3D-rendered world and a stranger story about control.

links.took: Jeppe Carlsen, a designer of Limbo, and its wordless puzzle design.
links.added: Worlds held inside orbs that you carry into other worlds.

links.took: Carlsen's puzzle design and wordless storytelling from Inside.
links.added: A top-down view and worlds nested inside one another.

links.took: Josef Fares' cooperative storytelling.
links.added: A co-op-only escape story for two players in split screen.

src.t: Wikipedia: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons

links.took: Its co-op-only design, which Hazelight wanted to expand on.
links.added: New mechanics in almost every level, framed as a romantic comedy.

src.t: Wikipedia: It Takes Two, citing IGN, 2020

links.took: The split-screen co-op formula with ever-changing mechanics.
links.added: Two writers trapped inside their own science fiction and fantasy stories.

links.took: Arrowhead's chaotic co-op and ever-present friendly fire.
links.added: Top-down military missions and stratagems called in with directional codes.

links.took: Top-down fantasy action against hordes of enemies.
links.added: Spells mixed from eight elements, with friendly fire and slapstick humor.

links.took: Stratagems, friendly fire and co-op missions for a satirical Super Earth.
links.added: Third-person shooting and a Galactic War shared by every player.

links.took: The core concept: an open survival world with creature companions.
links.added: Pals that work in your base, and guns.

src.t: Wikipedia: Palworld, citing Takuro Mizobe in TheGamer, 2021

links.took: Survival mechanics and in-game tasks.
links.added: Creature collecting and base automation with Pals.

src.t: Wikipedia: Palworld, citing Takuro Mizobe in TheGamer, 2021

links.took: Colony management, which Pocketpair cited as a major inspiration.
links.added: Pals as workers with needs in your base.

links.took: Catching wild creatures with a thrown sphere.
links.added: Guns, survival crafting and creatures put to work.
links.extra: Pocketpair says Pokémon wasn't a main inspiration; Nintendo and The Pokémon Company sued over catching-related patents in 2024.

links.took: Its publisher alleged parallels in gameplay loops and interface design.
links.added: A cozier management tone, as IGN put it.
links.extra: Movie Games investigated possible infringement, but no legal action followed; Vice argued such mechanics are common in the genre.

links.took: GTA III popularized a police wanted level that rises as you commit crimes in an open city.
links.added: A small-time drug business grown into an empire.

links.took: Sloclap's martial-arts combat know-how.
links.added: Aging with each death, and a single-player revenge story.

links.took: Sloclap's brawler experience, which the team said informed feel and precision.
links.added: Five-a-side football where each player controls one athlete.

links.took: Absolver's online technology.
links.added: Online football matches instead of martial-arts duels.

links.took: Fast, skill-based online team sport, cited by the team as an inspiration.
links.added: Football played on foot rather than with cars.

links.took: Team-based online play, cited by the team as an inspiration.
links.added: A third-person football match instead of a hero shooter.
